analyst_view.overall: Leaders Arsenal (28 points) host third-placed Manchester City (22) in the big game of the weekend. Arsenal threw away leads in a 2-2 at Newcastle and a 1-1 with Dortmund on Tuesday; Bukayo Saka (quad, about four weeks) and Martin Zubimendi (hamstring) are out, William Saliba is back, and David Raya's shoulder is still unclear, with Kepa as cover. City, in Enzo Maresca's first season, have one point from their last four league games and drew 2-2 with Napoli on Tuesday; Antoine Semenyo (knee) is out. The numbers now count Saka and Semenyo as out (about -10% on each side's goals) and referee John Brooks' high card rate, so my earlier goals cut for them is removed.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals: 1.4 for Arsenal and 0.9 for City, and they now take about 10% off each side for Saka and Semenyo. My earlier 5% cut was for those absences, so it is gone. Zubimendi's absence and Raya's doubt pull in opposite directions (less control for Arsenal, a weaker back-up keeper), so I stay at about 2.3.

corners.text: The numbers expect 10.0 corners, about even, already counting City's high corner count lately. Arsenal pile on pressure and win corners even without Saka, and City's open play gives up chances out wide, so nothing points clearly either way and I stay at about 10.

cards.text: The numbers expect 4.3 cards, already including John Brooks' high rate (4.4 a game) and Arsenal's rising card count. A title clash with City struggling against counter-attacks tends to bring tactical fouls, which the numbers have no stakes flag for, so I add a small 3%, to about 4.4.

shots.text: The numbers expect 24.5 shots, about even, and already count City allowing more shots than usual lately. Arsenal still take plenty of shots without Saka (30 against Dortmund), while City's possession game should limit them somewhat, so I stay at about 24.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers expect 7.8 shots on target. Arsenal have been taking many low-quality shots (4 of 30 on target against Dortmund, a game the league numbers do not see), and without Zubimendi, whom the numbers do not list, they lack a player who sets up clean chances, so I take about 3% off, to about 7.6.
